 # common.sh -- helpers shared by snapshot.sh, prune.sh and run-backup.sh.

+BACKUP_LIB_VERSION="1.5.0"

+# The umask moved out of snapshot.sh and up here on purpose. Every script in
+# the toolchain now writes something derived from the source tree -- prune.sh
+# lists it, run-backup.sh spools a manifest through /tmp -- and those two used
+# to run with whatever umask cron happened to hand them.
+umask 077

 log() {
   printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$*" >&2
 }
 
 die() {
   log "FATAL: $*"
   exit 1
 }
 
 require_cmd() {
   local cmd
   for cmd in "$@"; do
     command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $cmd"
   done
 }
 
 # epoch_of <path> -- mtime in seconds since the epoch.
 epoch_of() {
   local path="$1"
   case "$(uname -s)" in
     Darwin|*BSD) stat -f %m "$path" ;;
     *)           stat -c %Y "$path" ;;
   esac
 }
 
 # load_config <path> -- read KEY=VALUE lines and export the BACKUP_* ones.
 # Anything else is reported and skipped, so a stray line in an operator's
 # config file cannot overwrite PATH, HOME or IFS.
 load_config() {
   local path="$1" key value
   [ -r "$path" ] || die "config not readable: $path"
   while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
     case "$key" in
       ''|\#*)   continue ;;
       BACKUP_*) ;;
       *)        log "ignoring non-BACKUP key in config: $key"; continue ;;
     esac

   done < "$path"

+# Staging used to be snapshot.sh's business alone, but replication needs
+# somewhere to hold a finished-but-not-yet-published archive too.

+  local stage
+  stage="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/snapshot.XXXXXX")" ||
+    die "could not create a staging directory under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
+  printf '%s\n' "$stage"
+}
+
+# check_free_space <dir> <need_kb> <force> -- refuse to start a run that would
+# probably fill the archive filesystem. <force> carries the caller's --force /
+# BACKUP_FORCE setting; when it is on, a shortfall is logged and not fatal.
+check_free_space() {
+  local dir="$1" need_kb="$2" force="$3" avail_kb
+  avail_kb="$(df -Pk "$dir" | awk 'NR == 2 { print $4 }')"
+  case "$avail_kb" in
+    ''|*[!0-9]*) die "could not read free space for $dir" ;;
+  esac

+  if [ "$avail_kb" -ge "$need_kb" ]; then

+  fi
+
+  if [ "$force" ]; then
+    log "only ${avail_kb}KB free in $dir, wanted ${need_kb}KB -- continuing anyway"
+    return 0
+  fi

+  die "not enough space in $dir: ${avail_kb}KB free, need ${need_kb}KB (--force overrides)"

+# cat rather than scp so that a connection dropped mid-stream cannot leave a
+# partially transferred file sitting under the archive's final name.

+# servers the archive directory now holds tens of thousands of entries and the
+# expanded glob was overrunning the command line, so the same set is collected
+# with find instead: -maxdepth 1 keeps it as non-recursive as the glob was, and
+# -print0 keeps names with spaces intact. Ordering is unchanged.
+#
+# Two details keep the set identical to the glob's. The label is matched by the
+# `case` below rather than by `find -name`, because -name takes a pattern and a
+# label carrying *, ? or [ would have matched archives belonging to other
+# labels, where the quoted glob matched the label literally. And the start point
+# is "$dir/", with the slash: find does not descend a symlinked start point
+# without it, and an archive directory that is a symlink to a mounted volume is
+# a normal layout the glob expanded through.

   local dir="$1" label="$2" file
-  for file in "$dir/$label"-*.tar.gz; do
-    [ -f "$file" ] || continue
+  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
+    case "${file##*/}" in
+      "$label"-*.tar.gz) ;;
+      *) continue ;;
+    esac
     printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(epoch_of "$file")" "$file"
-  done | sort -rn | cut -f2-
+  done < <(find "$dir/" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tar.gz' -print0) |
+    sort -rn | cut -f2-

 # prune_label <dir> <label> <keep>
 prune_label() {
   local dir="$1" label="$2" keep="$3" file
   local idx=0
   while IFS= read -r file; do
     idx=$((idx + 1))
     [ "$idx" -gt "$keep" ] || continue
     rm -f "$file"
     log "pruned $file"
   done < <(list_archives "$dir" "$label")
   log "label=$label kept up to $keep of $idx archives in $dir"

 seen=""
 while IFS=$'\t' read -r epoch bytes path; do
   [ -n "${path:-}" ] || continue
   log "manifest record: epoch=$epoch bytes=$bytes archive=$path"
   if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
     log "manifest points at a missing archive, skipping: $path"
     continue

   base="$(basename "$path")"

   case "$seen" in
     *"|$dir/$label|"*) continue ;;
   esac
   seen="$seen|$dir/$label|"

item.text:
The patch disables rotation for the new manifest format and unintentionally forces the free-space override by default. It also introduces several reliability and confidentiality regressions in staging and remote replication.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Update prune to parse manifest v2 — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/snapshot.sh:101-101
  Every successful snapshot now emits four fields, but `prune.sh` still reads only `epoch bytes path`. Its `path` therefore contains the byte count plus the archive path, fails the `-f` check, and skips rotation, so archives accumulate beyond `BACKUP_KEEP`.

- [P1] Treat the default force value as disabled — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/lib/common.sh:81-81
  Without `--force` or `BACKUP_FORCE`, `snapshot.sh` passes the string `0`, which is nonempty and therefore makes this condition true. Every free-space shortfall is consequently downgraded to a warning by default, defeating the new disk-protection check.

- [P1] Follow symlinked source directories during the emptiness check — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/snapshot.sh:63-63
  When `BACKUP_SOURCE_DIR` is a symlink to a directory, it passes `-d` and previously worked with `tar -C`, but this `find` examines only the symlink at depth zero and emits nothing because of `-mindepth 1`. The run then exits 3 as a successful empty backup indefinitely; both this check and the later `du` calculation need to follow the directory target.

- [P1] Clean staging directories on every exit — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/snapshot.sh:77-77
  After staging is allocated, there is no longer an `EXIT`/signal cleanup trap. A failed `tar`, `mv`, or replication attempt therefore leaves a partial or complete archive in `TMPDIR`, and repeated scheduled failures can fill that filesystem.

- [P1] Publish replicas only after transfer completion — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/lib/common.sh:98-99
  If SSH disconnects after transmitting some bytes, the redirection has already created the archive under its final remote name and leaves it truncated. Because the local run then fails before publishing its manifest, nothing removes that remote artifact; write to a temporary remote path and rename it only after `cat` succeeds.

- [P1] Enforce private permissions on remote replicas — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/lib/common.sh:98-98
  On replicas whose noninteractive SSH shell uses the common `022` umask, `mkdir` creates a traversable directory and this redirection creates a `0644` archive, exposing potentially sensitive backup contents to other remote users despite the local `077` policy. Set a private umask or explicit permissions in the remote command.

- [P2] Quote remote paths before building the shell command — /private/var/folders/c1/l4z5k02n2779byvnymzxsvth0000gn/T/review-bench.ZCROs3/lib/common.sh:98-98
  When `BACKUP_REMOTE_DIR` or the label-derived archive name contains a single quote, interpolation terminates these shell quotes, causing replication to fail and potentially interpreting the remainder as remote shell syntax. Labels are otherwise unrestricted, so pass these values as safely quoted arguments rather than embedding them directly.
